newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares recover after falls, outlook healthy.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares recover after falls, outlook healthy.

text.p: Danish share prices recovered to close higher on Tuesday with the market giving a sigh of relief after recent U.S.-inspired plunges, with dealers more confident that the days ahead augured better.
"Even the Danish market's negative plunge on Monday after record U.S. declines was fairly moderate. The outlook looks healthy again now," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index gained 1.43 point to close at 182.29 in overall bourse turnover of 973 million crowns. The KFX September future rose 2.80 point to 182.80 with 402 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
The corporate interim result season dominated the market. ISS and BG Bank both turned in first-half 1997 results, the former closing two crowns higher at 210, the latter one up at 390.
Superfos put on six crowns to finish at 161 on the eve of its half-year results, but the most traded paper was Novo Nordisk which ended four higher at 701.
